sentences.text: The State, as well as the claimant, has preferred these appeals.
The State contends before us that the compensation awarded by the Reference Court is on a higher side, whereas the claimant is seeking enhancement of the amount.

2. The brief facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal are as follows:
An extent of 1.05 Ares of land in Survey No.1417/1 of Pattom Village in Thiruvananthapuram Taluk was acquired for the purpose of widening of Kesavadasapuram - Chalakuzhy road.
Section 4(1) notification was issued on 15.02.1999.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at Rs.3,34,334/- per Are.
Dissatisfied with the value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimant preferred application under Section 18 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Reference Court on purely a guess work and also considering the importance of the locality, fixed the land value at Rs.15 lakhs per Are.

The State contends before us in the appeal that & 547/22 2025:KER:21687 the claimant having failed to adduce any evidence to sustain her plea of enhancement, the Reference Court could not have fixed the land value purely on a guess work.
3. The claimant, on the other hand, has come up seeking for enhanced compensation, since according to her the value of the land acquired will come to Rs.25 lakhs per Are.

4. Heard, Sri.T.K.Shajahan - learned Senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the State and Sri.Sreekumar G. (Chelur) - learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimant.
5.
On a consideration of the rival submissions raised across the Bar, we are of the considered view that the State is entitled to succeed in its appeal.
A reading of the judgment rendered by the Reference Court reveals that the Reference Court has fixed the land value purely on a guess work.
The claimant thoroughly failed to produce any exemplars in order to enable the Reference Court to undertake the guess work.

Even if we are to assume that the Reference Court could have adopted the principles of guesstimation for the purpose of arriving at the market value of the land, in the absence of any evidence, purely on a guess work the Reference Court could not have fixed the land value.

6. At this point of time, learned counsel appearing for the claimant submitted that, if this Court finds that the claimant has & 547/22 2025:KER:21687 failed to adduce sufficient evidence to sustain her plea for enhancement, an opportunity will be granted to the claimant to substantiate her claim by producing sufficient evidence before the Reference Court.
We find that the said request is reasonable.
No doubt, the acquisition pertains to the year 1999.

However, the fact remains that the State Of Kerala vs Rajalekshmi Sreekumar on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128303541/
3 claimant is dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation granted by the Land Acquisition Officer and therefore, she has every right to substantiate her claim for enhanced compensation.
7.

sentences.text: Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the judgment and decree dated 18.07.2013 in LAR No.451 of 2009 cannot be sustained and therefore, the same is liable to be set aside.
In the result, LAA No.196 of 2015 preferred by the State is allowed.
The judgment and decree dated 18.07.2013 in LAR No.451 of 2009 is set aside.
Consequently, LAA No.547 of 2022 is allowed by way of remand.

The LAA No.451 of 2009 will stand restored to the files of II Addl. Subordinate Court,
Thiruvananthapuram.
The claimant is given an opportunity to adduce such evidence in order to substantiate her claim for enhancement.
Since we are remanding the matter back to the Reference Court, the parties shall appear before the Reference Court on & 547/22 2025:KER:21687 11.04.2025.
On appearance, the Reference Court shall endeavour to dispose of the reference case as expeditiously as possible.
It is brought to our notice that pursuant to the judgment and decree dated 18.07.2013, the State has deposited an amount of Rs.56,15,616/- before the Reference Court.
However, the claimant has not withdrawn the amount.

Since the State has deposited the amount of Rs.56,15,616/-, we make it clear that on remand, if the Reference Court finds that the claimant is entitled for any enhanced amount more than Rs.56,15,616/-, interest shall run only on such enhanced amount over and above the amount thus deposited by the State.

Since the claimant has preferred the appeal as an indigent person and since we are allowing her appeal by way of remand, it is made clear that she is under no obligation to remit the court fee in terms of the valuation in the appeal.
The claimant will be also free to seek release of the amount ordered as per the award by the Land Acquisition Officer.
Ordered accordingly.

Sd/-
